title: 🔊 "Qwen3" learns to speak — a synthetic voice that starts within 97 milliseconds!
body: 🔊 "Qwen3" learns to speak — a synthetic voice that starts within 97 milliseconds!
The company Together AI added a new model called "Qwen3" for text-to-speech — a model that turns any written text into spoken voice with a natural sound.
The model's most distinguishing feature is its speed: in streaming, the first audio segment starts within just 97 thousandths of a second — faster than the blink of an eye.
"Text-to-speech" technology is what makes voice assistants, audiobooks and robots talk to us, instead of being limited to writing.
"Streaming" means the voice starts before the whole sentence has finished generating, so the user feels the reply is instant, without annoying waiting.
These models are used in voice assistants, in reading articles to blind people, in dubbing videos, and in customer-service robots that talk to you on the phone.
Simply put: imagine writing a sentence and a human voice reads it to you within less than a tenth of a second. That is what the new "Qwen3" does.
Do you prefer AI to read articles to you in a voice, or to read them yourself?
